title: forecast_shift scratch tier array is sized by pipe_alive but filled by pipe_tier length — latent OOB write
evidence:
tiers := make([]u16, len(t.pipe_alive))
defer delete(tiers)
for i in 0..<len(t.pipe_tier) {
	tiers[i] = t.pipe_tier[i]
detail: Allocation bound (pipe_alive) differs from copy-loop bound (pipe_tier). If the two arrays ever diverge in length the copy writes past the slice. Safe today: both are appended in lockstep (core/topology.odin:187-191) and demolish only flips pipe_alive.
recommended_fix: Size the scratch by len(t.pipe_tier) (the bound the loop and tiers[ps] actually use), or copy into a len(t.pipe_tier)-sized allocation and index ps after an explicit bounds check.

title: routing_rebuild_with_tiers indexes caller-supplied tiers slice by live pipe slot with no length validation
evidence:
routing_rebuild_with_tiers :: proc(r: ^Routing_Table, t: ^Topology, cat: ^Catalogs, tiers: []u16, allocator := context.allocator) {
...
				nd := dist[cur] + cat.pipe_tiers[tiers[pi]].cost
...
				c := cat.pipe_tiers[tiers[pi]].cost
detail: New exported core proc reads tiers[pi] for every pi in 0..<len(t.pipe_alive) without checking len(tiers). Both current callers pass length-matched slices (t.pipe_tier[:] and the pipe_alive-sized scratch), so this is latent hardening, not a live read.
recommended_fix: Reject short views explicitly: if len(tiers) < len(t.pipe_alive) { return } (or clear r and return) at proc entry, so a future caller cannot pass an undersized hypothetical view.
